’s degree in Mechanical and Management Engineering.

learning_outcomes.text: Acquire basic skills in business and management engineering related to the sustainability of industrial investment projects.

Acquire basic notions of loan methods and capital repayment, analysis of investments in the private and public sector, project financing, public-private partnership techniques, financial statements, different taxation systems in Italy, and microeconomic aspects related to investment projects.

Equip students with fundamental skills for developing economic-financial models of investment projects in the industrial sector through project financing, for assessing their feasibility, and to verify the robustness of the results obtained through sensitivity and scenario analysis.
Understand the structures and economic-financial evaluations of investment projects in the private and public industrial sector as well as the sustainability of the same projects.
Apply the basic knowledge and understandings acquired in the industrial sector, with the support of problem-solving skills and basic quantitative tools.
Develop independent judgment in relation to the economic-financial evaluation of investment projects in the industrial sector.
Develop communication skills, in relation to the basic knowledge and understandings acquired, also with the aid of graphical and mathematical tools.

syllabus_topics: Introductory elements: choice problems; investments and costs; remuneration of unavailable money.
Interest: the loan transaction; cash flow diagram; simple interest; compound interest; nominal annual interest rate; effective interest rate.

Principles of economic and financial equivalence: equivalence concept; calculation of equivalence with a single factor; calculation of the equivalence with several factors; use of linear interpolation; financial tables.
Mortgages: add-on typology; mortgages loan typology; fixed interest rate mortgages; variable interest rate mortgages; mortgage balance; the financial bubble of subprime mortgages.
Bonds: investment opportunities; bonds and shares in comparison; zero coupon bonds; bonds with a payment coupon determined by interests; project bonds.
Inflation: price index; inflation rate; the effects on cash flows.

Analysis of private sector investments: investment decisions; accounting methodology; financial methodology; pay-back period; net present value (NPV); future value; annual equivalent; internal rate of return (IRR); minimum attractive rate of return; weighted average cost of capital; the classification of investment projects; the choice between the different investment alternatives: comparisons based on total and incremental values; the comparison between investment alternatives of different duration.

Investments in the public sector: public administration and social welfare; cost-benefit analysis: aggregate ratio, net ratio and Lorie-Savage ratio; cost-effectiveness analysis: fixed cost method and fixed effectiveness method.
Financial statements: characteristics and structure of financial statements; balance sheet; income statement.
Taxation systems in Italy: main taxes of the Italian system; tax on the income of physical persons; corporate income tax; value added tax: basic method and tax method.

Project financing: the profitability concept; type of works; economic and financial sustainability; public-private partnership; law references; viability test; economic and financial analysis; profitability indicators; debt coverage indicators; economic and financial model.
Microeconomics in the context of business and management engineering.
Perfect competition.
Elasticity.
Theory of consumer behavior.
Enterprise theory.
Selection of the investment project in the industrial sector.
Development of the economic-financial model in project financing: revenue projections; cost projections; income statement; cash flows.
Assessment of economic-financial feasibility.
Verification of the robustness of the results obtained: sensitivity analysis; scenario analysis.
assessment_rules: Learning verification is through a final examination consisting of a written test and a subsequent oral test. To be admitted to the oral test, a minimum score of 12/20 in the written test is required. The oral examination includes two questions and the presentation of a case study. The final grade, expressed in thirtieths, is obtained by summing the evaluations from both tests, with a minimum passing grade of 18/30. A written mid-term exam is available for attending students.
